summary: Old Forest Echoes (Ikimetsän kaiku) brings people closer to Finland’s old-growth forests through music and art created and performed among the trees. Led by Barbora Šilhánová — Barbora Xu — the project combines concerts, workshops, an album and documentary filmmaking to help protect threatened forests.

The music is rooted in four months spent in Finnish old-growth forests. Barbora is joined by artists including Wiebke Pandikow, Mikko H. Haapoja and Ville Tanttu, bringing land art, forest soundscapes and film into the work.

Working with the Finnish Nature League (Luonto-Liitto) and supported by the KONE Foundation, Old Forest Echoes raises awareness and funds for forest protection. Profits from album sales and donations are intended to help purchase a patch of old-growth forest for protection.

The project runs from January 2025 to April 2027, with a documentary planned for 2027. Audiences can experience the work in forest concerts and workshops, and in immersive indoor performances such as the Caisa concerts in Helsinki.
